own_solution.law: Long-solenoid inductance L = mu0 N^2 pi r^2 / l; steady current I = emf/R1 (zero-resistance winding shorts the second resistor); all stored energy L I^2/2 is dissipated in the second resistor after the switch opens

notes: L = 1.257e-6 x 800^2 x pi x 0.015^2 / 0.40 = 1.42164e-3 H. I = 12/4 = 3 A; E = 0.5 x 1.42164e-3 x 9 = 6.397e-3 J. With a 7.5 V battery added in series: I = 19.5/4 = 4.875 A, E = 0.5 x 1.42164e-3 x 23.7656 = 1.6893e-2 J. The second resistor's value sets only the decay time constant L/R2 (and carries no current in the steady state because the winding shorts it), so it cancels from the total heat. Earlier-run and torch-cell batteries are disconnected.
